title: Provider-neutral work-tracker seam with a GitHub adapter
summary: Adds a new `work_tracker` module to the osf crate: a provider-neutral `WorkTracker` trait (read items, write state, write recap, report capabilities) plus three helpers — the `Ready` dispatch rule, the finish-run write sequence, and an in-memory fake double. Alongside it lands the first adapter, `github_work_tracker`, which drives GitHub Issues and Projects v2 through the `gh` CLI: pure argv/payload builders, pure response parsers, a `RealGhRunner` with a timeout and an explicit-token identity gate, and a capability report derived from the project's status options. Three integration tests pin the fake run, the provider-neutrality of the seam, and the real runner's process behaviour.

nodes.label: Develop job
nodes.subtitle: picks one item, then reports
nodes.summary: The factory consumer that reads the tracker, picks a dispatchable item, and finishes the run with a state write and a recap. It reaches the tracker only through the `WorkTracker` trait.

nodes.label: WorkTracker trait
nodes.subtitle: read_items / write_state / write_recap / capabilities
nodes.summary: The seam itself: a provider-neutral trait plus the value types it moves — `WorkItem`, `WorkItemId`, `Status`, `Dependency`, `WorkState`, `BlockedCause`, `Capability`, `ReadOutcome`. Object-safe, so the factory holds a `&dyn WorkTracker`.

nodes.label: Ready rule
nodes.subtitle: pick / dispatchable
nodes.summary: Decides which read item may be dispatched: open, status Ready, every blocker closed. Returns `Pick::Item`, `NothingReady`, `NoneDispatchable` with per-item reasons, or `Unknown`. Kept out of every adapter so no adapter filters by status itself.

nodes.label: Finish run
nodes.subtitle: require_capabilities / finish_run
nodes.summary: The run's closing writes: check the needed states and the recap against the tracker's reported capabilities, then write the state, then the recap, stopping at the first failure and naming the step that failed.

nodes.label: FakeWorkTracker
nodes.subtitle: in-memory double
nodes.summary: An in-memory `WorkTracker` that records every call as plain data and does no I/O. Scriptable read outcome, capabilities, and per-operation or per-state failures, so a full factory run can be exercised without a process, file, network or clock.

nodes.label: GitHubWorkTracker
nodes.subtitle: Issues + Projects v2 over gh
nodes.summary: The first adapter. Each request is one `gh` invocation: argv and JSON payload built by pure functions, responses read by pure parsers. Reads verify the project's status field and options before paging items; writes resolve the project item id, post a cause comment for a blocked state, then move the single-select field.

nodes.label: GhRunner / RealGhRunner
nodes.subtitle: spawns gh, 60s timeout
nodes.summary: The process boundary. `RealGhRunner` spawns the program with piped stdio, drains stdout and stderr on their own threads, kills the child after a timeout, and returns trimmed stderr on a non-zero exit. It carries an optional token as its explicit identity.

nodes.label: argv & payload builders
nodes.subtitle: pure, pinned by tests
nodes.summary: Pure functions that build the argv and JSON body of every request: read items page, project status, item id, field mutation, and comment. The GraphQL query strings live here as constants.

nodes.label: response parsers
nodes.subtitle: pure, strict on ready items
nodes.summary: Pure parsers for each response: items page (with cursor and blocker paging), project status and options, project item id, and write result. A malformed item that is not in the ready status is kept as an `unreadable:` skipped item; a malformed ready item fails the page.

nodes.label: gh CLI
nodes.subtitle: installed program
nodes.summary: The installed GitHub command-line tool. Every adapter request is one invocation of it, fed a JSON body on standard input.

nodes.label: GitHub GraphQL API
nodes.subtitle: Issues + Projects v2
nodes.summary: The remote service behind `gh`: project items, single-select status fields, issue blockers, and issue comments.

edges.label: read_items / write_state / write_recap
edges.summary: The factory's whole use of the tracker goes through the trait; the develop job never names a provider.

edges.label: pick
edges.summary: The develop job asks the ready rule which read item it may dispatch.

edges.label: finish_run
edges.summary: The develop job closes the run through the finish sequence, which checks capabilities before writing.

edges.label: read_items
edges.summary: The ready rule reads items through the trait and applies the dispatch predicate itself.

edges.label: capabilities, write_state, write_recap
edges.summary: The finish sequence reads capabilities, then writes the state and the recap through the trait.

edges.label: impl WorkTracker
edges.summary: The fake double implements the trait in memory and records every call.

edges.label: impl WorkTracker
edges.summary: The GitHub adapter implements the trait over the `gh` runner.

edges.label: argv + payload
edges.summary: Every request the adapter makes is assembled by the pure builders.

edges.label: parse response
edges.summary: Every response the adapter reads goes through a pure parser.

edges.label: run(argv, stdin)
edges.summary: The adapter is a thin loop over the runner: one `gh` invocation per request, with the JSON body on standard input.

edges.label: spawn, piped stdio
edges.summary: The real runner spawns the installed program, feeds stdin, drains both pipes, and enforces the timeout.

edges.label: GraphQL / REST
edges.summary: The CLI turns each invocation into a GitHub API call.

views.title: Work-tracker seam and its first adapter
views.summary: The factory reaches a work tracker only through the provider-neutral trait; the ready rule and finish sequence sit on the seam, the fake double and the GitHub adapter sit behind it.

views.title: Inside the GitHub adapter
views.summary: The adapter is a thin loop: pure builders make the argv and payload, the runner spawns `gh`, and pure parsers read the response.
